Thoughtful 360° multi-view design enabling spatial awareness in constrained environments while maintaining 7 Hz inference speed for practical deployment
Large-scale training data collection (1.5M expert demonstrations) with multi-expert learning from specialized RL policies, providing substantial supervision for each navigation capability

weaknesses: Limited technical novelty—primarily an engineering combination of existing techniques (multi-expert learning, VQA training, VLA models) without significant methodological innovation; the core capability-balanced aggregation is a relatively straightforward heuristic weighted sampling approach

weaknesses: Limited technical novelty: Standard VLA architecture (visual encoder + LLM + action head), straightforward multi-view input design, and capability-balanced aggregation lack methodological innovation

Limited real-world evaluation: Only 4 primary deployment scenarios with qualitative metrics and ~20 trials per scenario; no evaluation on independent benchmarks or significantly different environments

Unclear contribution attribution: Improvements could stem from multi-view input (+?), larger RL data (+?), VQA co-training (+?), or architecture (+?); systematic ablation isolating each contribution is missing

Restrictive deployment assumptions: Requires 4 cameras for 360° observations; 7 Hz inference speed not compared with baselines
